newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-BAHAMAS' FUNES RUNS YEARS FASTEST 200M.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAHAMAS' FUNES RUNS YEARS FASTEST 200M.

text.p: Bahamian Olympian Sevatheda Fynes ran the year's fastest women's 200 metres on Wednesday, clocking 22.68 seconds in a preliminary race at the U.S. collegiate championships.
Despite unfavourable conditions, with temperatures only in the 60s, Fynes easily dominated her race, winning by almost six-tenths of a second.

"I was not surprised about my time," said the Michigan State University student, who helped the Bahamas win a silver medal in the women's 400-meter relay at the Atlanta Olympics. "I just wanted to get out there and do it."

The opening day of the four-day competition also produced the fastest women's 400-meter relay time in the world this year. A foursome of Louisiana State University athletes clocked 42.92 seconds in a preliminary race.
American Joey Woody of the University of Northern Iowa became the third-fastest 400-meter hurdler of the year in another preliminary as he ran 48.76 seconds.
Sweden's Mats Nilsson, a University of Alabama student, won the men's javelin final, throwing 74.90 meters (245 feet, 9 inches).

Jamaican Trecia Smith, who attends the University of Pittsburgh, claimed the women's long jump gold medal at 6.65 meters (21 feet, 10 inches) and Seilala Sua surprised fellow American and UCLA student Suzy Powell with a throw of 61.12 meters (200 feet, 6 inches) in the women's javelin.
Antother UCLA student, Mebrahtom Keflezighi of Eritrea, won the men's 10,000 meters in 28 minutes, 51.18 seconds.
